source.title: A study of uncertainty quantification in overparametrized high-dimensional models
source.authors: Lucas Clarté; Bruno Loureiro; Florent Krzakala; L. Zdeborová

record.file_problem: The full paper, including appendices, is present. There are minor formatting and math-extraction artifacts, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests double-descent behavior in a random-features classification model by varying overparameterization, using a different model and an asymptotic analysis rather than the original deep-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error curves against the parameter-to-sample ratio, including an unregularized estimator and optimally regularized estimators. It also reports calibration curves, which are a different measure from test error; those are recorded separately as findings that fit no version.
record.test_reason: The paper's focus is calibration, but its own asymptotic test-error curves for random-features logistic classification (Fig. 1 left) show double descent for λ→0+ ERM. They also show the peak removed under optimally tuned ℓ2 regularization. This is a new setting (random features, binary classification) with a result on V4 and V6, not a replication of the original method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find that Bayesian and ERM estimators reach very similar test error, and that unregularized ERM shows test-error double descent that optimal regularization makes monotonic. Calibration shows a double-descent-like peak that optimal regularization does not remove, giving an accuracy–calibration trade-off. Empirical Bayes with evidence maximization is well calibrated. ERM tuned on error plus temperature scaling gives both the best error and good calibration, while the Laplace approximation is unreliable.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes asymptotic binary classification with random features, varying p/n; it does not reproduce the original deep-network size, epoch, or sample-count experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Test-error shape depends on regularization: the unregularized ERM shows double descent, whereas the authors say optimally regularized ERM test error becomes monotonic. The additional zero-label-noise setting is plotted, but its test-error curve shape is not described in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Calibration Δ0.75 peaks near the interpolation threshold for λ→0+ and λerror estimators, and this peak persists under optimal regularization. Temperature scaling or evidence maximization removes it, and it is absent in the zero-noise n/d=10 setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In random-features classification, calibration error versus overparameterization can show a double-descent-like peak at interpolation that optimal regularization does not remove.

fits_no_version.finding: The variance of the Bayes-optimal predictor conditioned on the estimator's confidence shows a bump near the interpolation threshold that persists under optimal regularization and after temperature scaling (Fig. 1 right, Fig. 2 right).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pointwise uncertainty (conditional variance) can show double-descent-like non-monotonicity in overparameterization even when test error is monotonic.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
record.problems: The main curves are presented in figures without numerical curve values or uncertainty intervals. The model is a Gaussian-input random-features classification setting without feature learning; the authors identify lack of feature learning as a limitation. The additional zero-noise test-error curves are not described as to their shape in the text.

untested.parts: No deep networks; random features only, with no feature learning.
No sweep over training epochs; the study gives asymptotic minimizers only.
Sample count n/d is fixed per figure; there is no sample-wise sweep near the threshold.
Only random-features logistic classification on Gaussian data; no other model classes.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across axes.
Does not test whether label noise drives the peak; the zero-noise test-error curves are plotted but not described. No triple or multiple descent examined.

missing.what: Test-error curves in a second low-noise setting (τ0=0, n/d=20, ||θ*||²=50) for ERM at λ=1e-4, λerror and λloss, EB, and BO. The shape is not described in the text.
Conditional-variance curves that show a double-descent-like bump; these are not recorded as rows.

record.verdict_notes: The test-error double descent and its removal by optimal regularization are presented as known results (citing Gerace et al. 2020 and Nakkiran et al. 2021), but they are recomputed here in the paper's own asymptotic analysis. The interpolation threshold is the linear-separability point. All curves are figure-only, with no numeric values in the text. The zero-noise appendix settings could bear on V6's noise dependence, but the text says nothing about their test-error shape.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses random features, not deep networks.
No sweep over training epochs or training time.
No sweep that increases the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
Tests random-features binary classification only; does not establish whether the curve holds across model classes generally.
Does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Tests regularization effects on test error and reports results in settings with different label noise, but does not establish that noise drives the peak or test for triple or multiple descent.
Does not remeasure complexity using an effective parameter count.
